# The Magisterial deck

**What it rewards:** Playing the draft. Its strength comes from combinations of cards the player finds while drafting, from boons paid on draft, and from culture, great people of every family, great-person works and wonders. A single card is modest; the right set of abilities together is strong. **Directions inside it:** a reroll and pass engine; a deep collection beyond the chairs; boons and random gifts; culture converted into whatever the empire lacks; great-person works arranged to claim land; wonders that pay across the empire.

*Initially generated by `scripts/deckDocs.mjs`; now a hand-edited design spec (deck-list pass, 2026-10-06).*

**Review (2026-10-06).** Target 45 to 55 exclusive cards. Before this pass: 91. After: 46 (8 / 12 / 12 / 11 / 3 across Tiers 0 to IV), with four commissions. The reconciliation of the six sheets (2026-10-06) made The New Code (Dominion's wording) and The Rising Nave (Devotion's wording) shared cards and cut this sheet's twins of both, and cut the shared The Imperial Examinations and Triumphal Arches. Most cuts were cards doing the same job as another card: five "culture buildings give +X each" cards, eight "great-person works pay flat yields" cards, and five "cities containing a wonder gain X" cards, each now reduced to one or two. The balance pass (2026-10-06) restored Looted Art as a card shared with Dominion (13 shared cards now), cut nothing exclusive, and changed the text of twelve cards, among them The Archive, The Swearing-In, The Antechamber, Civic Granaries, The Masters' Domain and The Honoured Dead; the deck stays at 46 exclusive cards. The deck's three arcs:
- **The draft-action engine.** Cheap or free draft actions paired with cards that pay for each action: The Second Reading, The Critics' Circle and The Patient Eye open it; The Rotating Chairs, The Swearing-In, The Open Door and The Accessions Register build it; The Salon des Refusés, The Archive, The Antechamber and The Senate Charter deepen it; Officials by Merit and The Patron's Choice bend it late; The Grand Salon, The Hall of Wonders, The Disputation and The Long Deliberation are its Tier IV. The Court Painter opens a draft payer at Tier 0.
- **The collection and its boons.** Cards drafted for what they give at once, and cards that pay for every Order held: Gifts at Court, then The Wandering Muse and The Unveiling, then The Encyclopedia and The Archive, then The Grand Lottery and The Cabinet of Curiosities, ending in The Universal Library, The Polymath's Study and The Grand Retrospective.
- **Works and wonders.** Great-person works of any family placed to claim and arrange land, and wonders that pay the empire: The Laureate, The Landmark Bounds and The Guild of Masons, then The Quarter of Masters, The Siting Masters and The Golden Age, then The Masters' Domain, The Wonder Commonwealth and Commission: The Paradise Garden, ending in The Magister's Court, The Last Commission, The Processional Way, The Pull of the Masters, Commission: The Ideal City, The Envious Eye, The Bulwark of Marvels and The Royal Invitation. The Cornerstone and The Markstones open it at Tier 0.

The culture engine and conversion (The Repertory, The Temple of the Muses, The Working Court, The Learned Patron, The Commissioned Works) sit under all three.

**Tier 0 and Tier IV pass (2026-10-07):** added 3 Tier 0 and 12 Tier IV cards. Tier 0 gains an opener for the works-and-wonders arc (The Cornerstone), a first draft payer that feeds great people (The Court Painter) and a first territory card (The Markstones); the deck's early faith is The Temple of the Muses, already at Tier 0. Tier IV adds no card toward Opus production, since The Magister's Court, The Universal Library and The Last Commission already fill that quota. Instead it carries each arc to full size: the draft-action engine (The Grand Salon, The Disputation, The Long Deliberation, The Hall of Wonders), the collection (The Polymath's Study, The Grand Retrospective), works and their arrangements (The Processional Way, The Pull of the Masters, Commission: The Ideal City), and the late wonder race and the Opus's defence (The Envious Eye, The Bulwark of Marvels, The Royal Invitation).

- **built**: exists in the game as written.
- **revised**: exists, and this sheet changes it; the last column says what it was.
- **new**: proposed on this sheet; the last column says whether an existing effect shape fits or what new mechanic it needs.
- **deferred**: in the data but not dealt; the note says why.
- **cut**: listed only under Proposed cuts.

**Words this sheet uses.**
- A **hand** is a draft offer. **Drafting** takes a card from it. **Passing** gives the whole hand up. **Rerolling** pays to have it dealt again. **Seating** puts a card you hold into a chair; **unseating** takes it out.
- A **reward hand** is a free Order hand dealt by an event or a card, outside the culture meter.
- Your **collection** is every Order you hold, seated or not.
- **On draft** means the card pays once, when you take it. Some boon cards do nothing while seated; they still count toward cards that read your collection.
- A **commission** is a goal card: seat it, reach the goal, take the reward, and it leaves its chair. Commissions pay no beads.

**Draft-action families.** Each draft action has cards that let you take it more often or more cheaply, and cards that pay you each time you take it. None of them names another card.
- **Reroll.** Enablers: The Second Reading (the first reroll of each hand is free), The Salon des Refusés (reroll with culture), and The Temple of the Muses (faith, which pays for rerolls). Payers: The Critics' Circle, The Disputation (science equal to the reroll's faith price, even when free), Commission: The Salon Season. Faith from Devotion and gold from Commerce's The Brokers' Redraw also pay for rerolls. Officials by Merit trades the whole family away for bigger hands.
- **Pass.** Enablers: The Patient Eye (a pass refunds culture), The Archive (keep one card from a passed hand, which then counts as a draft rather than a pass). Payers: The Unwritten Chapter, The Long Deliberation (renown), Commission: The Salon Season.
- **Draft.** Enablers: The Open Door (hands cost less), Officials by Merit and The Hall of Wonders (larger hands), The Subscription List (gold into the draft pool), and every reward-hand card. Payers: The Court Painter and The Accessions Register (a charter counts for both), the shared The Art Dealers (gold), and every boon card.
- **Seat and unseat.** Enablers: The Rotating Chairs (shorter seals), The Antechamber (an extra chair while held). Payers: The Swearing-In (once per card per government), The Senate Charter's Assembly Hall (pays per filled wildcard chair), and The Patron's Choice (reseating it changes what it pays).
- **Reward hands.** Sources: The Unveiling (wonders), the shared The New Code (captures), The Grand Lottery, The Envious Eye (a rival's wonder), Commission: The Salon Season and Commission: The Ideal City. They are drafts, so the draft payers read them.
- **Every family at once.** The Grand Salon raises every card that pays for a draft action by half, without naming any of them.
- **The collection.** Pure boon cards (Gifts at Court, The Wandering Muse, The Grand Lottery, The Cabinet of Curiosities, and the shared The Sword of State) and The Archive grow the collection without taking a chair. The Encyclopedia, The Universal Library, The Polymath's Study (the different decks in it) and The Grand Retrospective read it.

Counts cover the cards exclusive to Magisterial; shared cards are listed separately. Cut cards are not counted. The Golden Age and The Magister's Court are revised but still deferred, and are counted as deferred.

Deep enough for eleven chairs: 46 exclusive cards and 15 shared ones are available by Tier III, with 15 more at Tier IV. Magisterial's own chair cards (The Antechamber, Commission: The Wonder of the Age) add only a little to the demand.

Wonders feeding the draft: more choice for the rerolls, passes and The Archive to work on. Scientific pair: bigger hands show more charters. |
| **The Bulwark of Marvels** | uncommon | new | The city building your Magnum Opus gains +4 strength and +25 hit points for each wonder you hold, at most +24 strength and +150 hit points. | Pressure and interaction: defending your own Opus. Needs: a scope for "the city building the Magnum Opus" (The Universal Library needs the same scope); the strength and hit-point lines fit the existing `cityStat` shape, counted on wonders held. A deck with a weak army still has to hold its Opus city through the last wars; this lets its wonders do that. |
| **The Pull of the Masters** | rare | new | At the start of each turn, each of your great-person works takes one tile beside it that belongs to a rival and that no rival city is working. A city centre and a rival's own great-person works are never taken. | Pressure and interaction: territory taken through works. Needs: a land claim that can take a rival's tile (The Landmark Bounds takes only unowned tiles), swept over your works in tile order so the result is deterministic. A work has six neighbours, so the card's reach is set by where works are placed. Dominion pair: citadels count as works and already claim land. |
| **The Royal Invitation** | rare | new | Any great person of yours, of any family, may be spent beside a rival city that is building the Magnum Opus. That city puts half as much production toward the Opus for 5 turns. Each rival can be slowed this way once every 15 turns. | Pressure and interaction: slowing a rival's Opus. Needs: a new act open to every great-person family while the card is seated (`grantsAbility` lets a card open a verb), and a timed effect on the rival's city (`City.timed`, an absolute expiry turn). From history: Francis I bringing Leonardo da Vinci to France, and other rulers luring a rival court's masters away. It slows only production; gold and faith poured into the rival's Opus are untouched. |
| **The Envious Eye** | uncommon | new | When a rival completes a wonder you were building, the production you had put into it moves to the next item in that city's queue instead of being refunded as gold, and you are dealt a free Order hand. | Pressure and interaction: the late wonder race. Needs: reward hands (shared with The Unveiling), and a transfer of the production in a lost wonder (today it refunds gold, `wonderRefundGoldPerHammer`, and only for the front row; this card keeps that rule about which row counts). Losing a race stops being a disaster for the deck that races for every wonder. |
| **Commission: The Ideal City** | rare | new | Commission. Goal: one of your cities holds two wonders and works three great-person works. Reward: that city claims every unowned tile within three hexes and gains +25% culture, science and production for the rest of the game; you are dealt two free Order hands. Then it leaves its chair. | Big moment. Needs: commissions; reward hands; the land claim shared with The Landmark Bounds; a lasting city effect granted by a commission (Commission: The Wonder of the Age needs a lasting grant too). Captured wonders count, so a rival finishing the last wonders does not close the goal. From history: the Renaissance ideal city (Pienza, Palmanova), a town planned whole around its monuments. |
| **The Grand Retrospective** | rare | new | On draft: your capital gains 20 culture, 20 science and 20 production for each wonder, great-person work and Order you hold. Seated, this card does nothing. | Big moment: one decisive turn paid by all three arcs at once. Needs: on-draft boons (shared with Gifts at Court). The payment is one windfall per yield, so no modifier raises it. A late empire with eight wonders, eight works and fifteen Orders gains 620 of each. It still counts toward cards that read the collection. |
| **The Disputation** | rare | new | Each time you reroll an Order hand, gain science equal to that reroll's faith price, whatever you paid it with, even if it was free. | Late signature: the reroll family at full size. Needs: a reroll occasion that carries the hand's faith price. Pays for free rerolls (The Second Reading), culture rerolls (The Salon des Refusés) and gold rerolls (Commerce's The Brokers' Redraw) alike, so each enabler becomes science without the card naming any of them. Devotion pair: faith spent on rerolls comes back as science, the deck's weak essential. |
| **The Long Deliberation** | uncommon | new | Each time you pass on an Order hand, gain renown equal to half the culture the hand cost. | Late signature: the pass family at full size. Needs: the pass occasion (shared with The Unwritten Chapter). A late hand costs a few hundred culture, so a pass brings a great person noticeably closer. A hand kept through The Archive counts as drafted and pays nothing here. |

## Synergies with other decks

### Dominion: the triumph
- **What each gives.** Dominion gives great generals and citadels, which Magisterial's any-family cards pay on like any other work, and captured cities full of buildings and wonders. Magisterial gives boons that fill an army's gaps (a random great person, production on draft), culture turned into production, and wonders that pay across the empire.
- **Hooks Magisterial creates:** great-person works of any family, wonders, reward hands, on-draft boons (the shared The Sword of State gives a unit). **Hooks it reads from Dominion:** captured cities (The New Code, Looted Art), citadels (every card that pays on a great-person work), garrisons (Examinations of State).
- **Shared improvements:** citadels. A citadel counts toward Commission: The Paradise Garden and Commission: The Patron's Gallery like any other work.
- **Cards on this sheet that serve the pair:** Gifts at Court, The Wandering Muse, The Working Court, The Laureate, The Masters' Domain, The Honoured Dead, Commission: The Patron's Gallery, The Pull of the Masters (citadels count as works), Commission: The Ideal City (captured wonders count), The Bulwark of Marvels (holds the Opus city through the last wars); shared: The Sword of State (a unit on draft; the pair's Tier I card), The New Code, Looted Art, Examinations of State.

### Expansionist: shaping territory
- **What each gives.** Expansionist gives room: claimed and tended land to place works on, in the patterns Magisterial's arrangement cards reward. Magisterial gives culture (Expansionist's gap) and territory: works that claim the land around them.
- **Hooks Magisterial creates:** great-person works that claim land (The Landmark Bounds, Commission: The Paradise Garden). **Hooks it reads from Expansionist:** tended tiles, which count as sides of a paradise garden; works placed side by side on claimed land (The Quarter of Masters); forests, hills and water beside works (The Siting Masters); farms beside works (The Sculpted Landscape).
- **Shared improvements:** manufactories (paid on by every any-family work card), and landmarks beside tended land.
- **Cards on this sheet that serve the pair:** The Landmark Bounds, The Siting Masters, The Quarter of Masters (taken from the Expansionist sheet), Commission: The Paradise Garden, The Masters' Domain, The Markstones, The Processional Way (a line of works needs land laid out for it); shared: The Sculpted Landscape, Garden Provinces, Garden Cities. The landscape-garden idea (tended land that pays culture) belongs on the Expansionist sheet; this sheet leaves it there.

### Commerce: the art market
- **What each gives.** Commerce gives gold that buys draft actions, and merchants and customs houses for the any-family cards. Magisterial gives culture turned into gold, and boons that save purchases.
- **Hooks Magisterial creates:** draft actions that can be bought (The Subscription List pays gold into the draft pool; The Brokers' Redraw's gold rerolls feed The Critics' Circle and Commission: The Salon Season). **Hooks it reads from Commerce:** gold (The Subscription List, and the shared The Art Dealers, which pays it for every draft), foreign routes (Travelling Players, The Cosmopolitan Court).
- **Shared improvements:** customs houses, and landmarks on trade routes (The Cosmopolitan Court pays gold on works).
- **Cards on this sheet that serve the pair:** The Subscription List, The Performers' Treasury, The Critics' Circle, Commission: The Salon Season, The Commissioned Works, The Disputation (gold rerolls pay science at the faith price); shared: The Art Dealers (the pair's Tier I card), Travelling Players, The Cosmopolitan Court.

### Devotion: the cathedral
- **What each gives.** Devotion gives faith, which is what rerolls cost today, so a Devotion empire is the natural engine for the reroll family; and holy sites. Magisterial gives wonders, culture, and boons that include faith.
- **Hooks Magisterial creates:** wonders and great-person works; faith from culture buildings (The Temple of the Muses) and faith on draft (The Grand Lottery). **Hooks it reads from Devotion:** faith spent on rerolls (The Critics' Circle), holy sites (Sacred Commissions), great people spent (The Last Commission, Sacred Patronage), wonders and Cathedrals in progress (The Rising Nave).
- **Shared improvements:** holy sites and landmarks.
- **Cards on this sheet that serve the pair:** The Temple of the Muses, The Grand Lottery, The Second Reading, The Critics' Circle, The Golden Age, The Disputation (faith rerolls come back as science); shared: The Rising Nave, Sacred Commissions, Sacred Patronage.

### Scientific: the academy
- **What each gives.** Scientific gives charters, which are drafted and so count as drafts, and scholars and academies for the any-family cards. Magisterial gives more drafts and rerolls, so Scientific sees more charters and can reroll for the one it needs.
- **Hooks Magisterial creates:** rerolls and extra choice in a draft (The Second Reading, The Open Door, Officials by Merit, The Antechamber). **Hooks it reads from Scientific:** charters as drafts (The Accessions Register), academies (The Quarter of Masters, The House of Wisdom), libraries (Illuminated Treatises).
- **Shared improvements:** academies and landmarks (The Quarter of Masters pays when any two works stand together).
- **Cards on this sheet that serve the pair:** Officials by Merit, The Encyclopedia, The Accessions Register, The Learned Patron, The Senate Charter, The Open Door, The Court Painter (a charter counts), The Hall of Wonders (bigger hands show more charters); shared: The House of Wisdom, Illuminated Treatises.

## Shared cards for the user to rule on

Only one of the two sheets recommends a change to these, so each stays on both shelves until the user rules.
- **Garden Provinces** (with Expansionist): Magisterial recommends cutting it, because it is a flat yield on a condition that is nearly always true. Expansionist does not comment.

Illuminated Treatises (with Scientific) and Garden Cities (with Expansionist) were on this list; both were kept by the user (2026-10-12), because every pair of decks keeps a shared card at Tier I or earlier (`docs/flags.md` item (qqqqqq) 14).
